limitations.name: Data limitation
limitations.note: Training data is scarce, biased, or narrow (language, accent, subtype).

limitations.name: Clinical governance limitation
limitations.note: The tool needs supervision that the design does not guarantee.

limitations.name: Generalizability limitation
limitations.note: Small or single site samples, not yet broadly applicable.

limitations.name: Construct validity limitation
limitations.note: The tool may not measure what it claims to measure.

limitations.name: Accessibility limitation
limitations.note: Cost, hardware, or digital literacy barriers to real world use.

limitations.name: Nosological boundary limitation
limitations.note: The tool targets a condition adjacent to, but distinct from, aphasia.

patterns.name: N-ary relation (Descriptions & Situations)
patterns.note: ClinicalApplication reifies a tool's use instead of a single direct triple, so it can carry a subtype, a domain, an evidence level and a limitation all at once.

patterns.name: Classification pattern
patterns.note: AphasiaType classifies a clinical profile under a diagnostic category, not a physical object — the same role a 'Concept' plays in classification-style ontologies.

patterns.name: Orthogonal taxonomy
patterns.note: Limitation is split into 6 disjoint kinds that cut across the clinical taxonomy: one application can carry limitations of several natures at once.

patterns.name: Defined class for automatic recognition
patterns.note: UndifferentiatedByAphasiaSubtype is derived from a cardinality restriction, not typed in by hand — see the note below on how it is actually evaluated.

patterns.name: Property chain for derived navigation
patterns.note: toolTargetsAphasiaType composes hasClinicalApplication with targetsAphasiaType, so a reasoner can link a tool straight to a subtype without a new triple ever being asserted by hand.

patterns.name: Cardinality integrity constraints
patterns.note: Every ClinicalApplication is now required to have exactly one source tool, exactly one evidence level, and at least one declared limitation — checked against all 40 real instances before being asserted as a rule.

patterns.name: A second defined class, built the other way round
patterns.note: HighEvidenceApplication is defined from declared values (owl:hasValue), not from an absence like the first defined class — so a reasoner infers its 4 members correctly, with no open-world caveat needed.

patterns.name: External alignment to ICF (WHO)
patterns.note: Linguistic domains and communication modalities carry explicit ICF codes (e.g. OralComprehension → b1670), mapping each local class onto a recognised external clinical standard.

negativeCQs.name: Did tool X get more accurate between its 2022 and 2024 version?
negativeCQs.note: Not answerable: the graph has no time dimension on its measurements, only one snapshot per clinical application.

negativeCQs.name: Why is heterogeneity (I²) so much higher for covert/consciential tools?
negativeCQs.note: Not answerable as an inference: the graph states that the I² values differ, not why — causal explanation stays in the written meta-analysis, not the axioms.

negativeCQs.name: Which applications have no declared limitation at all?
negativeCQs.note: A query can run, but an empty result would mean 'not yet annotated', never 'proven limitation-free' — OWL's open-world assumption blocks that reading.

negativeCQs.name: Which single subtype does a mixed clinical profile belong to?
negativeCQs.note: Not answerable by design: the leaf syndromes are declared mutually disjoint, so a reasoner would flag an inconsistency before giving a single answer.
